regimen_profiles.regimen_role: Maintenance after a response to platinum chemotherapy
regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: Oral PARP-inhibitor maintenance after a complete or partial response to platinum. Distinguish first-line advanced high-grade disease from platinum-sensitive relapsed high-grade serous disease.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: Maintenance after a response to platinum chemotherapy
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Niraparib: Niraparib blocks proteins that help repair damaged DNA. This can slow the growth of some cancer cells.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Take the prescribed dose once every day. A 28-day cycle is a way of recording treatment. There is no planned tablet-free week.
key_points: The NCCP lists blood pressure at week 2, monthly for 6 months and then every 3 months. The European product information calls for at least weekly readings for the first 2 months, monthly during the first year and periodically thereafter. Agree a written monitoring plan with your team before starting.

PRIMA studied first-line maintenance after platinum response. The risk of progression or death was lower with niraparib than placebo in the homologous-recombination-deficient group (HR 0.43, 95% CI 0.31–0.59). NOVA separately studied maintenance after platinum-sensitive relapse.
The first-line and relapse studies enrolled different populations. Delayed progression is a group result and does not establish a survival benefit for an individual.
Follow your prescribed anti-sickness plan. Bedtime dosing may help nausea. Speak to the team before changing the dose or stopping.
Show your team all medicines, including blood thinners, aspirin and supplements. Do not stop prescribed medicines on your own.
Niraparib can harm a developing baby. Discuss contraception, fertility and breastfeeding before starting.
regimen_profiles.review_status: Feasibility build; independent oncology, pharmacy and patient review pending

regimen_profiles.regimen_role: dMMR/MSI-H advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer
regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: First-line treatment for dMMR/MSI-H primary advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer. Six combination cycles are followed by single-agent dostarlimab maintenance.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: dMMR/MSI-H advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Dostarlimab: It removes a brake on immune cells so they can recognise and attack cancer. It can also cause inflammation in healthy organs. Paclitaxel: It disrupts cell division. Hair follicles, blood cells and nerves can also be affected. Carboplatin: It damages DNA in dividing cells. Kidney function helps determine the prescribed amount.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Three medicines every 3 weeks for six planned cycles. The first Jemperli-only visit is 3 weeks after cycle six. After that, Jemperli is given every 6 weeks.
key_points: Immune inflammation can start between visits or after treatment ends. Keep the immunotherapy alert card and show it to every team caring for you.
In RUBY, adding dostarlimab to chemotherapy and then continuing dostarlimab reduced the hazard of progression or death in the dMMR/MSI-H group (HR 0.28, 95% CI 0.16–0.50).
These results compare groups over time. They cannot predict the duration of benefit for one person. The NCCP indication shown here is biomarker-specific.
Carboplatin carries high sickness risk. Follow the scheduled anti-sickness medicines and the rescue plan given by your team.
Before paclitaxel the unit provides medicines to reduce allergic reactions. Confirm any doses you must take at home before attending.
Sickness risk is minimal with Jemperli alone. Ask which medicines continue once chemotherapy ends. Keep carrying your immunotherapy alert card.
